requirements.requirement: Mount /tmp and /dev/shm with nosuid, nodev, and noexec so setuid behavior, device-node access, and program execution are ignored.
requirements.summary: Both paths were directly observed as tmpfs mounts with nosuid,nodev,noexec. Before and after restart, executable probes returned 126 and device-node reads failed; both directories retained mode 1777.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the hardened mount settings survive a reboot.
requirements.summary: The node was healthy before restart, the reboot was acknowledged and observed through a connection reset, and the boot ID changed. Afterward the system returned to running state, both hardened mounts and persistent fstab entries were present, and enforcement tests passed again. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use an implementation compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were identical before and after execution. The implementation used native fstab, mount, and systemd facilities; package health remained clean and no package installation or platform replacement occurred.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Both mounts enforce the requested restrictions, a directly observed reboot demonstrated persistence and recovery, the provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1, and the OS release and kernel were preserved.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the complete command timeline. The fstab changes and live mounts directly implemented the task; the retained /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening file is an intentional rollback backup created with the implementation, not unexplained residue. Probe files and device nodes were bounded verification artifacts and were removed. The reboot was required to prove persistence and satisfy the provider restart protocol. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, no damaged package state, and no material new network exposure; temporary-file differences are normal reboot regeneration.
